entry.title: Ignition credentials belong in your secrets manager
entry.summary: Gateways still hold database passwords and script secrets. Why that breaks rotation and audits, and how a native secret-provider module resolves them from Vault, Azure, AWS or Google instead.

entry.title: Put your Ignition gateway on the same dashboards as everything else
entry.summary: OpenTelemetry and Prometheus for Ignition 8.3: curated metrics, logs, and no wrapper.conf surgery.

entry.title: Tag history that stays fast when retention gets long
entry.summary: TimescaleDB-backed historian for Ignition 8.3. Aggregates in tens of milliseconds over hundreds of millions of rows.

entry.title: Stop scripting RabbitMQ inside Ignition
entry.summary: Named AMQP broker connections as gateway config, Event Streams and system.amqp scripting. Replaces the client parked in getGlobals().

entry.title: Page the channel the crew actually watches
entry.summary: Teams, Slack and webhook alarm notification profiles for Ignition 8.3, with acknowledgement, retry, fallback and a delivery audit trail.

entry.title: Fourteen Perspective components the platform never shipped
entry.summary: Free Apache-2.0 components: scheduling board, calendar, editable grid, pan-and-zoom, branching diagram, and the admin family Vision had.

entry.title: Yes, your Ignition gateway can run Doom
entry.summary: A free Perspective component that runs Doom inside SCADA. Tags fire the shotgun, alarms pause the marine. Industrially useless on purpose.

entry.title: A dark Ignition Designer from one menu item
entry.summary: Free FlatLaf dark mode for the Ignition 8.3 Designer. Tools → Dark Mode, remembered between launches, open source on GitHub.

entry.title: Ignition modules for the gaps the platform leaves
entry.summary: Secrets, RabbitMQ, Timescale, OpenTelemetry, alarm channels, Perspective UI, Designer dark mode, and Doom: Ignition 8.3 modules from Mustry, and where each one fits.

entry.title: MQTT and Sparkplug B: why factories stopped polling
entry.summary: Polling sets a ceiling on every factory data project. MQTT flips the direction; Sparkplug B adds the contract that makes it an architecture instead of topic soup.

entry.title: MES vs SCADA vs historian: what actually goes where
entry.summary: Three layers of a factory's data stack, each answering a different question, and most stalled data projects got the layering wrong.
